newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt privatising 20 percent of drugs firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt privatising 20 percent of drugs firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state said on Wednesday it wanted to sell 20 percent of the equity in Cairo Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries in a partial privatisation worth at least 28.3 million pounds ($8.3 million).

The state holding company National Pharmaceuticals said that for three days starting November 17 it would offer 708,000 shares of the 3.54 million shares at a minimum price of 40 pounds a share -- a P/E ratio of 7.3.

It has set aside five percent for individuals, five percent for companies, investment funds and financial institutions, and 10 percent for the Employee Shareholder Association, which holds shares on behalf of the employees. The allocation to individuals may be increased if there is demand.
The final price will be decided through the "price discovery" mechanism used in the Egyptian stock exchange.

The exchange first used the same mechanism for the partial privatisation of General Silos and Storage this month. Those shares were sold at 39.00 pounds, a little above the minimum bid of 37.00 pounds.
